title: The Odes and Psalms of Solomon
author: J. Rendel Harris (trans)
description: The Odes and Psalms of Solomon, published from the Syriac version by J. Rendel Harris (Cambridge University Press, 1909; second edition 1911), with introduction, translation and notes. Harris, the Quaker biblical scholar and manuscript hunter, discovered in 1909 a Syriac manuscript among his own papers containing the forty-two Odes of Solomon, previously known only from quotations in the Pistis Sophia, together with the eighteen Psalms of Solomon. The Psalms of Solomon are Jewish poems of the first century BCE lamenting Pompey's capture of Jerusalem and longing for the Davidic Messiah. The Odes, probably composed in Syria around the late first or early second century CE, are the earliest Christian hymnbook: ecstatic songs of union with the Lord, the living water, the crown of truth, the Word and the descent into Hades, with mystical and proto-Gnostic tones. Harris's discovery was a sensation and the Odes are central to the study of early Christian mysticism and liturgy.
